events.title: Walmart beat revenue forecasts at $188.8B with e-commerce up 17% and raised its yearly outlook for a third time, though US growth slowed.
Anthropic priced its upsized IPO at $83 a share, above its range, raising about $81.3B in the largest offering on record; ANT trades from Nov 19.
Nvidia closed 2.9% lower at about $151 despite beating forecasts, as CEO succession and China risk weighed; AMD rose 5.3% and Broadcom 3.7%.
Neocloud shares including CoreWeave and Iren fell alongside Nvidia after its results failed to lift sentiment.
Minutes of the Oct 27-28 meeting showed nearly all officials expect a quarter-point hike in December and a couple saw room for a larger move.
Target posted 5.6% comparable sales growth, its best in five years, raised its full-year sales outlook and its shares rose about 7%.
Lowe's beat profit forecasts with comparable sales up 1.8%, helped by about $250M of tariff refunds, and trimmed its margin outlook.
Anthropic is reportedly telling investors its IPO will price at the top of the $70 to $78 range or higher, ahead of Nov 18 pricing.
Home Depot beat sales forecasts with comparable sales up 2.2%, nudged up its profit outlook and named a new CEO, but shares slid over 3%.
UnitedHealth shares fell about 4.7% on renewed concern over Medicare Advantage payments and rising medical use.
Nvidia reported quarterly revenue of $115.8B, up 103% on the year, and guided to $130B next quarter with gross margin easing to 71-72% and no China data-center sales assumed.
October retail sales rose 0.2%, slowing from 0.8% in September, as car dealer sales fell 1.6% while online sales rose 1.2%.
Effingham County, Georgia approved the site plan for OpenAI's $20B Project Camellia data center and tabled a data-center moratorium until January.
China and Canada expanded tariff relief on seafood, pork and some steel and aluminum after Carney met Xi, as US-Canada talks remain unresolved.
Nasdaq-100 futures fell about 1% before Nvidia's first earnings without Jensen Huang, with the 10-year Treasury yield at 5.15% and the index down about 8% in a month.
Anthropic plans to price its IPO of 825 million shares at $70 to $78 on Nov 18 and start trading as ANT on Nov 19, with up to 20% set aside for retail buyers.
Futures put the odds of a Dec 9 rate hike at 100%, up from 67% a week earlier, after October payrolls rose 165,000 and unemployment held at 4.1%.
The high-yield spread narrowed from 342 to 320 basis points between Nov 6 and Nov 12 even as the 2-year Treasury yield jumped from 4.51% to 4.86%.
Eli Lilly agreed to buy privately held blood-cancer biotech Calytrix Bio for up to $1.5B in cash including milestone payments.
Effingham County, Georgia commissioners are due to vote Nov 17 on site plans for an OpenAI data center and on a proposed data-center moratorium, after two postponements.
Nvidia fell 4.1% to about $156 on Nov 16, dragging the Nasdaq down 2.5% and the Dow down over 700 points before its earnings.
PJM asked federal regulators to halve grid connection studies for data centers to about a year and show states what upgrades cost.
Former ambassadors said a Canada-US trade deal is possible but US tariffs on Canadian goods may stay in place.
TensorWave signed a six-year deal to supply OpenAI with 457 MW of AMD-based AI capacity across several US sites.
The US and China held their first trade council meeting on Nov 13, discussing a proposed $60B package of reciprocal tariff cuts ahead of a Trump-Xi meeting in Shenzhen.

nvidia.news: Nvidia beat forecasts on Nov 17 with $115.8B of revenue, up 103% on the year, and guided to $130B, but the shares closed 2.9% lower near $151 on Nov 18 as CEO succession and China risk weighed and margins are guided down to 71-72%.

labs.news: Anthropic priced its upsized IPO at $83, above the range, raising about $81.3B in the largest offering on record (Nov 18); ANT starts trading Nov 19. OpenAI signed a six-year 457 MW AMD-based capacity deal with TensorWave (Nov 16).
cons: $1T+ valuation leaves little room for error
labs.weak: The labs now carry public-market valuations that depend on chip and cloud spending staying funded.

bigtech.news: Nvidia's strong results and higher guidance (Nov 17) confirm hyperscaler orders are holding, but tech shares kept selling off on Nov 18 with the 10-year yield at 5.1%. Fed minutes (Nov 18) back a December hike.

cloud.news: CoreWeave and Iren fell with Nvidia after its results (Nov 18); the high-yield spread widened to 3.47% (+0.18 in 30 days). ERCOT demand is up 2.6% and PJM 1.6% on the year, and Dallas, TX is 100% in severe drought and Prince William and Loudoun in Northern Virginia are now 100% and 99.8% in drought, up sharply in four weeks.

citizens.news: Effingham County, GA approved OpenAI's $20B site plan and put off a moratorium to January (Nov 17), angering residents. Household electricity prices are up 5.4% and energy 21% on the year; Dallas, TX is 100% in severe drought and Prince William and Loudoun in Northern Virginia are now 100% and 99.8% in drought, up sharply in four weeks. The saving rate is 3.8%.

spacex.news: Merger talks with Tesla continue toward a possible December announcement; Musk said on Nov 18 he should not get Tesla awards from a merger. Gas is $3.10, ERCOT demand is up 2.6% on the year, and Dallas County is 100% in severe drought.

tesla.news: Merger talks with SpaceX continue (Nov 12, Nov 18). Vehicle sales are flat at a 16.0M rate and October car dealer sales fell 1.6% (Nov 17).

consumer.news: No notable Apple news this week. Consumer sentiment was 48.1 in September, down 13% on the year, and a December rate hike is expected.

retail.news: Target's comparable sales rose 5.6%, its best in five years (Nov 18), and Walmart raised its outlook a third time with e-commerce up 17% (Nov 19); Lowe's beat on tariff refunds. October retail sales rose only 0.2%, up 6.8% on the year (Nov 17).

autos.news: Car dealer sales fell 1.6% in October, dragging retail sales (Nov 17); vehicle sales are flat at a 16.0M rate and used car prices are down 3.3% on the year. A December hike would raise loan costs.

fashion.news: Shoppers cut clothing purchases in October (Nov 17); apparel prices are up 3.5% and imports from Vietnam up 61% on the year.

education.news: No notable news this week. Student loans stand near $1.78T in the latest (dated) data and higher rates raise borrowing costs.

banks.news: BBB spreads are 1.16% (+0.08 in 30 days) and high-yield 3.47% (+0.18), near one-year highs, and lenders remain wary of AI debt. Banks underwrote Anthropic's record $81.3B IPO (Nov 18).

fed.news: Target range is 3.75-4.00% with fed funds at 3.88%; core PCE is 3.1% against the 2% goal, unemployment 4.1% and the mortgage rate 7.11%. Minutes released Nov 18 show nearly all officials expect a December hike and a couple saw room for a larger move.

chips.news: AMD rose 5.3% and Broadcom 3.7% on Nov 18 even as Nvidia fell; OpenAI's TensorWave deal adds AMD-based capacity (Nov 16).

power.news: No new power deals this week. Gas is $3.10 (-0.12 in 30 days) and grid demand is up 1.6% in PJM and 2.6% in ERCOT on the year.

healthco.news: UnitedHealth fell about 4.7% on Medicare Advantage concerns (Nov 17), while Lilly is still riding obesity-drug data and its Calytrix deal (Nov 12-16). Medical care prices are up 1.9% on the year.

industrials.news: No notable news this week on Boeing, Caterpillar or Lockheed Martin. The freight index is down 3.0% on the year.

payments.news: Strong Target and Walmart results (Nov 18-19) point to steady card volumes. Consumer credit is up 3.0% on the year and card delinquency 2.85%.

trade.news: China and Canada expanded tariff relief after Carney met Xi (Nov 17), and Trump met Xi and Carney in Shenzhen (Nov 18-19) without announced US deals. Imports from China are up 34%, Mexico 40% and Vietnam 61% on the year.
